correctness.rationale: For the closed two-simplex, the coordinate z=(3(x0+x1)-2)+i√3(x0-x1) rescales Euclidean differences by constant √6. Direct symbolic derivation gives ż=−2z−bar(z)^2/4. Its radius obeys r′≤−2r+r²/4; since all simplex points have r0≤2, scalar comparison gives R(t)=8/(1+3exp(2t)). For two solutions, the factored difference equation w′=−2w−(bar(z1)+bar(z2))bar(w)/4 gives |w|′≤(−2+R/2)|w|; integration yields G(t)=16e^{2t}/(1+3e^{2t})². On z=−r the scalar exact solution r(t;r0)=8r0/[r0+(8−r0)e^{2t}] has derivative at r0=2 precisely G(t), so distinct initial pairs approaching that boundary vertex saturate the Lipschitz supremum. The proof includes t=0 and distinguishes supremum from attainment. Independent symbolic derivative and sample ODE checks support the analytic comparison.
